knowledge:
- key_parameters: scale_views=logical indicating whether to scale views to unit variance (default FALSE) ;; scale_groups=logical indicating whether to scale groups to unit variance (default FALSE) ;; num_factors=integer specifying the number of factors to train ;; likelihoods=character vector specifying the likelihood per view ("gaussian", "poisson", "bernoulli") ;; spikeslab_factors=logical indicating whether to use spike-slab sparsity prior on factors (default FALSE) ;; spikeslab_weights=logical indicating whether to use spike-slab sparsity prior on weights (default TRUE/FALSE depending on setup) ;; ard_factors=logical indicating whether to use ARD prior on factors (default TRUE for multi-group) ;; ard_weights=logical indicating whether to use ARD prior on weights (default TRUE for multi-view) ;; maxiter=integer specifying maximum training iterations (default 1000) ;; convergence_mode=character specifying convergence speed/strictness ("fast", "medium", "slow") ;; use_basilisk=logical indicating whether to use basilisk to manage the python environment (default TRUE)
- alternatives: PCA is mentioned as a linear comparison (MOFA factors are interpreted similarly to principal components but handle multi-omics and missing values). Downstream, non-linear dimensionality reduction methods like t-SNE or UMAP can be run on the learned factors.
- when_to_use: Use when you have multi-modal measurements (multi-omics) derived from the same samples, with a relatively large sample size (at least ~15 samples). It is appropriate for uncovering global sources of variation across multiple views/groups, or modeling smooth variation along a covariate (like time) using MEFISTO.
- pitfalls: Non-gaussian likelihoods (Poisson, Bernoulli) can give non-optimal results; the docs strongly recommend transforming count data (e.g., size factor normalization + variance stabilization/log transform) to continuous measurements and using Gaussian likelihoods. Feature selection is critical: select highly variable features (HVGs) per assay before fitting to ensure faster training and robust inference, especially to reduce feature imbalance between views. Python integration: MOFA2 connects to the mofapy2 Python package via reticulate or basilisk, which is the source of most installation/running problems. Multi-group functionality is advanced and discouraged for beginners.

workflows.name: standard_mofa_analysis
workflows.intent: Train a standard multi-omic factor analysis model on multiple data modalities and perform downstream visualization and data extraction.
input: data (a list of matrices with features as rows and samples as columns)
dt (a long data.frame with columns sample, feature, view, value)
workflows.stages:
1. Create MOFA object using create_mofa.
2. Define data, model, and training options using get_default_data_options, get_default_model_options, and get_default_training_options.
3. Prepare the MOFA object using prepare_mofa.
4. Train the model using run_mofa.
5. Perform downstream analysis including variance decomposition (plot_variance_explained), factor visualization (plot_factor, plot_factors), weight visualization (plot_weights, plot_top_weights), data heatmaps/scatters (plot_data_heatmap, plot_data_scatter), non-linear dimensionality reduction (run_umap, run_tsne, plot_dimred), and data extraction (get_factors, get_weights, get_data).
workflows.code:
MOFAobject <- create_mofa(data)
MOFAobject <- create_mofa(dt)
plot_data_overview(MOFAobject)
data_opts <- get_default_data_options(MOFAobject)
model_opts <- get_default_model_options(MOFAobject)
model_opts$num_factors <- 10
train_opts <- get_default_training_options(MOFAobject)
MOFAobject <- prepare_mofa(
  object = MOFAobject,
  data_options = data_opts,
  model_options = model_opts,
  training_options = train_opts
)
outfile = file.path(tempdir(),"model.hdf5")
MOFAobject.trained <- run_mofa(MOFAobject, outfile, use_basilisk=TRUE)
model <- load_model(filepath)
plot_data_overview(model)
samples_metadata(model) <- sample_metadata
head(get_variance_explained(model)$r2_total[[1]])
head(get_variance_explained(model)$r2_per_factor[[1]])
plot_variance_explained(model, x="view", y="factor")
plot_variance_explained(model, x="view", y="factor", plot_total = TRUE)[[2]]
plot_factor(model, factor = 1:3, color_by = "age", shape_by = "condition")
p <- plot_factor(model, factors = c(1,2,3), color_by = "condition", dot_size = 3, dodge = TRUE, legend = FALSE, add_violin = TRUE, violin_alpha = 0.25)
p <- p + scale_color_manual(values=c("A"="black", "B"="red")) + scale_fill_manual(values=c("A"="black", "B"="red"))
print(p)
plot_factors(model, factors = 1:3, color_by = "condition")
plot_weights(model, view = "view_0", factor = 1, nfeatures = 10, scale = TRUE, abs = FALSE)
plot_top_weights(model, view = "view_0", factor = 1, nfeatures = 10)
plot_data_heatmap(model, view = "view_1", factor = 1, features = 20, cluster_rows = TRUE, cluster_cols = FALSE, show_rownames = TRUE, show_colnames = FALSE)
plot_data_scatter(model, view = "view_1", factor = 1, features = 5, add_lm = TRUE, color_by = "condition")
set.seed(42)
model <- run_umap(model)
model <- run_tsne(model)
plot_dimred(model, method = "TSNE", color_by = "condition", dot_size = 5)
views_names(model) <- c("Transcriptomics", "Proteomics")
factors_names(model) <- paste("Factor", 1:get_dimensions(model)$K, sep=" ")
factors <- get_factors(model, factors = "all")
weights <- get_weights(model, views = "all", factors = "all")
data <- get_data(model)
factors <- get_factors(model, as.data.frame = TRUE)
weights <- get_weights(model, as.data.frame = TRUE)
data <- get_data(model, as.data.frame = TRUE)

workflows.name: mefisto_covariate_analysis
workflows.intent: Train a covariate-aware factor model (MEFISTO) to capture smooth variation along a continuous covariate (e.g., time) and interpolate factors.
input: dd$data (a list of matrices containing multi-omic data)
time (a covariate matrix with samples in columns and one row containing the covariate values)
workflows.stages:
1. Create MOFA object using create_mofa.
2. Set covariates using set_covariates.
3. Define data, model, training, and MEFISTO options using get_default_data_options, get_default_model_options, get_default_training_options, and get_default_mefisto_options.
4. Prepare and train the model using prepare_mofa and run_mofa.
5. Perform downstream analysis to relate factors to covariates (get_scales, plot_factors_vs_cov, plot_data_vs_cov) and interpolate factors (interpolate_factors, plot_interpolation_vs_covariate).
workflows.code:
sm <- create_mofa(data = dd$data)
sm <- set_covariates(sm, covariates = time)
data_opts <- get_default_data_options(sm)
model_opts <- get_default_model_options(sm)
model_opts$num_factors <- 4
train_opts <- get_default_training_options(sm)
train_opts$maxiter <- 100
mefisto_opts <- get_default_mefisto_options(sm)
sm <- prepare_mofa(sm, model_options = model_opts, mefisto_options = mefisto_opts, training_options = train_opts, data_options = data_opts)
outfile = file.path(tempdir(),"model.hdf5")
sm <- run_mofa(sm, outfile, use_basilisk = TRUE)
plot_variance_explained(sm)
r <- plot_factor_cor(sm)
get_scales(sm)
plot_factors_vs_cov(sm, color_by = "time")
df <- plot_factors_vs_cov(sm, color_by = "time", legend = FALSE, return_data = TRUE)
plot_weights(sm, factors = 4, view = 1)
plot_top_weights(sm, factors = 3, view = 2)
plot_data_vs_cov(sm, factor=3, features = 2, color_by = "time", dot_size = 1)
sm <- interpolate_factors(sm, new_values = seq(0,1.1,0.01))
plot_interpolation_vs_covariate(sm, covariate = "time", factors = "Factor3")
